result.question: Intel Arc A770 (DG2, PCI 8086:56a0) running llama.cpp's SYCL backend (oneAPI 2026.1 DPC++ / Unified Runtime Level Zero adapter, intel-compute-runtime NEO 26.35.39758, Level Zero loader 1.32) on Linux kernel 7.3-rc1 (Arch, tkg build), switching between the i915 and xe kernel drivers. Research four things. (1) How the xe and i915 KMDs interact with the Level Zero / compute-runtime user-mode stack that llama.cpp SYCL uses: submission model differences (execlists vs GuC, LR-mode VMs / long-running compute queues and user fences on xe, drm_sched job timeouts, preempt timeouts, VM_BIND), how copies on the blitter/copy engine (bcs) are ordered against compute (ccs) via events on each driver, and any known xe issues with DG2 where a copy-engine memcpy chain stalls or the blitter hits 'Engine reset: engine_class=bcs … Timedout job' with an xe devcoredump showing RING_ESR=0x1 and IPEHR=0xfffff000 (observed here; workaround found: UR_L0_USE_COPY_ENGINE=0). Look for bug reports in intel/compute-runtime, intel/llvm (unified-runtime), freedesktop drm/xe gitlab, and kernel lists that match. (2) Concrete driver differences that could explain both a large prefill throughput gain (+6-17% dense, +55-62% MoE) and a decode slowdown or per-copy latency increase under xe versus i915 on DG2: GT frequency governors and min_freq defaults (xe floors at RPe 750 MHz, i915 at RPn 300), RC6/idle behaviour, ULLS/direct submission support, page-table/VM_BIND costs for many small host-to-device copies, immediate command lists, counter-based events. (3) Firmware: which GuC/HuC/DMC/GSC blobs each driver loads for DG2 (xe uses i915/dg2_guc_70.bin and dg2_dmc_ver2_08.bin, no HuC entry; i915 loads dg2_huc_gsc.bin via mei_gsc/mei_pxp), whether newer GuC 70.x releases than 70.53.0 exist in the linux-firmware git tree or Intel's firmware repository, how to install newer blobs on Arch (linux-firmware-git, manual /usr/lib/firmware override, xe.guc_firmware_path/huc_firmware_path), and whether xe will ever support HuC on DG2 (needed for VAAPI VBR/CBR encode). (4) Recommended configuration for best llama.cpp interactivity on each driver: kernel parameters and module options (i915.enable_guc, i915.request_timeout_ms, xe.force_probe, xe.probe_display, xe.wedged_mode, CONFIG_DRM_XE_JOB_TIMEOUT_MAX/PREEMPT_TIMEOUT Kconfig, sysfs engine job_timeout_ms/preempt_timeout_us/timeslice_duration_us, ccs_mode / multi-CCS), GT frequency pinning via sysfs, PCIe ASPM, and the user-mode knobs that matter for SYCL llama.cpp on Arc (UR_L0_USE_COPY_ENGINE, UR_L0_USE_IMMEDIATE_COMMANDLISTS, UR_L0_USE_DRIVER_INORDER_LISTS, SYCL_PI_LEVEL_ZERO_*, NEO debug keys like EnableDirectSubmission / DirectSubmissionRelaxedOrdering, ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN, GGML_SYCL_* build and runtime options), plus Intel's own guidance (llama.cpp docs/backend/SYCL.md, oneAPI release notes, compute-runtime docs). Prioritise primary sources: kernel source and docs, intel/compute-runtime and intel/llvm repositories and issues, linux-firmware commit history, llama.cpp docs and issues from 2025-2026. Distinguish DG2 (Alchemist) from Battlemage/Lunar Lake findings explicitly.
result.summary: On an Arc A770 (DG2) the i915 and xe drivers load byte-identical GuC firmware (i915/dg2_guc_70.bin, v70.53.0, shipped by linux-firmware since tag 20251111 and still current in linux-firmware main and Arch as of 2026-09-29), so the observed i915-vs-xe behaviour differences (prefill gain, decode slowdown, bcs "Timedout job") cannot be attributed to the GuC blob version; they stem from how the two KMDs drive the same GuC. The structural difference that matters for the Level Zero/SYCL stack is that compute-runtime always creates xe VMs in LR (long-running) mode with USER_FENCE syncs, the xe exec ioctl carries no BO list and adds zero kernel-side dependencies between execs, and eviction uses preempt fences plus a rebind worker, whereas on i915 NEO passes a full residency list and the kernel implicitly serialises via dma-resv; cross-engine bcs-to-ccs ordering under xe is therefore entirely the UMD's job (L0 events / GPU-side semaphores), and xe fronts GuC with a 1:1 drm_sched whose per-engine-class job_timeout_ms is hard-capped at CONFIG_DRM_XE_JOB_TIMEOUT_MAX=10000 ms (rebuild the tkg kernel to raise it) and whose preempt_timeout_us defaults to 640 ms. No upstream bug report was found that matches the DG2 signature (bcs reset, RING_ESR=0x1, IPEHR=0xfffff000); the nearest analog is compute-runtime #999 (Battlemage B65, GuC consumes a bcs context but never dispatches it, -62 timeout), while the two plausible xe fixes examined (USM-reserved-BCS timestamp WARN, resubmit-signalled-jobs suspend race) are either not applicable to DG2 or already in 7.3-rc1 and not steady-state. A newer DG2 GuC, v70.74.0 (UAPI 1.38.4), exists only in the intel-staging branch of gitlab.com/kernel-firmware/drm-firmware (MR !84, merged 2026-09-02) and can be dropped in at /usr/lib/firmware/i915/dg2_guc_70.bin without renaming because both drivers only match the major version and accept newer minors silently; HuC on DG2 under xe remains unsupported upstream (no VAAPI CBR/VBR low-power encode), with only a stalled out-of-tree v4 patch proposing it. Every claim about GT frequency governors, SLPC, and sysfs frequency pinning explaining the decode slowdown was refuted, so question (2) is largely unanswered by verified evidence.

findings.claim: Under xe, the Level Zero/compute-runtime stack runs in a structurally different submission model from i915: NEO unconditionally creates the VM with DRM_XE_VM_CREATE_FLAG_LR_MODE, attaches exactly one DRM_XE_SYNC_TYPE_USER_FENCE out-sync per exec, and waits via DRM_IOCTL_XE_WAIT_USER_FENCE; the xe exec ioctl accepts no buffer-object list and, for LR-mode VMs, adds zero kernel-side dma-resv dependencies between execs, so ordering of a blitter copy (bcs) against a compute kernel (ccs) is the UMD's responsibility (L0 events / GPU-side semaphore waits), not the KMD's. Eviction/rebind for these VMs is done by preempt fences (queue suspended before eviction) and a rebind worker rather than at exec time. On DG2 specifically (no has_usm), an A770 NEO VM is necessarily LR + non-fault = preempt-fence mode. On i915, by contrast, NEO passes the full residency list with EXEC_OBJECT_PINNED and the kernel performs implicit dma-resv serialisation across BOs and engines, every request carries a timeout-bounded dma_fence, and there is no user-fence uAPI at all.
findings.evidence: Kernel xe_cs doc: 'forcing the user to use in / out fences on every exec rather than the kernel tracking dependencies of BO' and 'Rebinds / dma-resv usage applies to non-compute mode VMs only as for compute mode VMs we use preempt fences and a rebind worker'. drm-vm-bind-async doc defines long-running workloads as needing a mode that 'disallows completion dma-fences' and memory/user fences that 'do not necessarily obey the dma-fence rule'. xe_drm.h documents LR_MODE as 'no upper time limit on job execution time' and forbids syncobj out-syncs there; xe_guc_submit.c exempts LR jobs from the drm_sched timeout check. NEO ioctl_helper_xe.cpp getFlagsForVmCreate() sets LR_MODE unconditionally; exec uses sync[0].type = USER_FENCE, SIGNAL only. xe_exec.c guards every dma-resv step with !xe_vm_in_lr_mode(); xe_vm.c has preempt_rebind_work_func; xe_pci.c graphics_xehpg (DG2) lacks has_usm so FAULT_MODE returns -EINVAL. i915: i915_gem_execbuffer.c has no preempt_fence/rebind_work/LR_MODE; i915_request.h embeds a dma_fence; upstream i915_drm.h has zero 'user_fence' hits; NEO's i915 waitUserFence is a stub. Merged claims [2],[3],[4], all 3-0.

findings.claim: Scheduler architecture differs in a way that changes timeout and preemption behaviour: on DG2 stock i915 already uses GuC submission (uc_expand_default_options defaults to ENABLE_GUC_SUBMISSION for Gen12+ except TGL/RKL/ADL-S), so preemption/timeslicing are GuC firmware policies, but i915 never adopted the DRM scheduler (its Kconfig does not select DRM_SCHED; intel_guc_submission.c uses i915's own i915_sched_engine + tasklet, and the 2021 RFC's 'convert to DRM scheduler' phase was abandoned); the i915 watchdog is the global i915.request_timeout_ms (default 20000 ms). xe is effectively GuC-only (xe_device_uc_enabled() returns true unconditionally, force_execlist modparam removed, execlist backend has NIY stubs) and fronts GuC with drm_sched in a 1:1 scheduler:entity mapping (num_rqs=1, one drm_gpu_scheduler per exec queue, .timeout=MAX_SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT for LR queues), with TDR via guc_exec_queue_timedout_job and per-engine-class job_timeout_ms. The meaningful DG2 contrast is therefore i915_sched_engine+GuC vs drm_sched(1:1)+GuC+LR-mode, not GuC vs execlists.
findings.evidence: RFC text verbatim: 'these features are not required for GuC submission as the GuC does these things for us' and 'Remove in-order completion assumptions from DRM scheduler ... so it is possible for jobs to finish out of order'. Verifiers grepped current master: zero drm_sched references in i915 GuC/execlists code; xe Kconfig selects DRM_SCHED; xe_guc_submit.c pushes timeslice/preempt timeout as GuC KLVs (__guc_exec_queue_policy_add_execution_quantum / _preemption_timeout) and hooks timedout_job = guc_exec_queue_timedout_job; drm_sched_get_finished_job() still assumes in-order pending_list, which xe sidesteps via the 1:1 mapping rather than by removing the assumption. Claim [8] passed 2-1 because its wording 'rather than by the kernel's DRM scheduler' is imprecise for i915 (which never used drm_sched); the substantive division of labour is verified against source. Claim [9] passed 3-0.

findings.claim: No upstream bug report was found that matches the DG2 signature (xe, bcs 'Engine reset ... Timedout job', devcoredump RING_ESR=0x1, IPEHR=0xfffff000). The nearest analog is intel/compute-runtime issue #999 (opened 2026-09-17, OPEN, 'Needs Feedback'): on Battlemage Arc Pro B65 (8086:e222, NOT DG2) under xe with GuC 70.72.1 on kernel 7.1.8, a bcs context is consumed by GuC via H2G SCHED_CONTEXT but never dispatched (LRC ring tail advances, head stalls, engine idle, no page fault), and ~108 s later the job is timed out as 'not started' (error -62) with a GT reset; that devcoredump shows an idle engine, not an execution error, so it is the same failure shape but a different mechanism signature. Two other candidate xe defects were examined and ruled out for this case: (a) the June 2026 fix for engine_id_to_hwe() WARN_ONCE / stale context timestamps on the USM-reserved highest BCS instance used by the kernel migrate engine only applies on has_usm platforms (PVC/Xe2/Xe3; DG2 has no has_usm, migrate shares BCS0 with user queues) and is already merged in 7.3-rc1; (b) the 6.12.36 / v6.16 fix 'drm/xe/sched: stop re-submitting signalled jobs' is a suspend/resume (s2idle/s3/s4) or post-GT-reset race that re-runs freed jobs (DMAR faults, CAT errors), is already in 7.3-rc1, and is not a steady-state copy-engine ordering defect.
findings.evidence: #999 body (verified via gh issue view): 'the LRC ring head never advances, the engine stays idle, no page fault occurs, and ~108 s later the job times out as not started (error -62)'; trace xe_sched_job_run -> xe_sched_job_timedout 108.7 s later; dmesg 'trying reset from guc_exec_queue_timedout_job'. Single reporter, mechanism is reporter inference, only Intel reply is a template request. Rodrigo Vivi's 2026-06-09 patch 'drm/xe/lrc: fix spurious warning when reading context timestamp': 'class:instance 3:8 is XE_ENGINE_CLASS_COPY on the highest BCS instance, which xe_hw_engine.c reserves for USM'; 7.3-rc1 xe_lrc.c already has engine_valid_for_utilization(); xe_hw_engine.c sets num_paging_engines only if has_usm and xe_pci.c graphics_xehpg lists only BCS0 without has_usm. ChangeLog-6.12.36 (commit 0ee54d5cacc0): 'a race between suspend cancelling the worker that processes the free_job()'s ... on resume ... drm_sched_resubmit_jobs() ... run_job() on everything still on the pending_list'; corroborated by Ubuntu LP #2115392 where the identical bcs Timedout splat appeared only under fwts s3 tests. Confidence medium because the core statement is an absence-of-evidence result and claim [1] passed only 2-1.
findings.vote: 3-0, 2-1, 3-0 (merged [0],[1],[7]); a related claim that the June 2026 TDR patch changed early-return to GT reset was refuted 1-2

findings.claim: DG2's GuC is a single blob at i915/dg2_guc_70.bin that BOTH i915 and xe load (xe has no xe/dg2_* file; modinfo xe lists only i915/dg2_guc_70.bin and i915/dg2_dmc_ver2_08.bin for DG2, modinfo i915 adds i915/dg2_huc_gsc.bin). The shipped version is GuC 70.53.0 (UAPI/compat 1.26.0, CSS build date 2025-10-27): drm-firmware MR !43 (Julia Filipchuk, Intel) bumped DG2 from 70.49.4 to 70.53.0 on 2025-11-04, cherry-picked into linux-firmware main as f2a23165 on 2025-11-06 (MR !770), first in tag 20251111; Arch shipped it from linux-firmware 20251111-1 and this host's pacman.log confirms the upgrade on 2025-11-11. As of 2026-09-29 linux-firmware main WHENCE still lists 70.53.0 for DG2, current Arch extra/linux-firmware is 20260916-1, the installed linux-firmware-git 20260929.33b68e2c-1 blob decodes to 70.53.0, and xe debugfs gt0/uc/guc_info reports wanted 70.53.0 / found 70.53.0 / compat 1.26.0. Both drivers' firmware tables want 70.53.0 (xe_uc_fw.c: fw_def(DG2, GT_TYPE_ANY, major_ver(i915, guc, dg2, 70, 53, 0)); intel_uc_fw.c: fw_def(DG2, 0, guc_maj(dg2, 70, 53, 0))). Consequently the GuC blob version by itself cannot explain any i915-vs-xe difference on this machine; the two KMDs configure the same GuC differently (ADS/policies, SLPC min freq, LR-mode queues, timeouts).
findings.evidence: MR !43 WHENCE diff: 'File: i915/dg2_guc_70.bin -Version: GuC API/APB ver 70.49.4 for DG2 +Version: GuC API/APB ver 70.53.0 for DG2'; commits e2dd7bce (i915: DG2, MTL) and cae6dd6a (xe: BMG, LNL, PTL) — the xe-side commit touches only xe/bmg,lnl,ptl_guc_70.bin. Upstream WHENCE xe/ entries: lnl, bmg, ptl, nvl only. Local blob sha256 e6e3f8b4... decompressed, CSS sw_version 0x00463500 = 70.53.0, submission_version 0x00011a00 = 1.26.0. /proc/cmdline has only i915.force_probe=!56a0 xe.force_probe=56a0, no guc_firmware_path override. If testing is successful the binary blobs will replace the major versioned *_guc_70.bin files'. i915 BAT passed, i915 full CI had failures on unrelated RKL/SNB/TGL shards, xe KUnit 761/0. findings.claim: Installing a newer 70.x DG2 GuC on Arch is a drop-in file replacement with no renaming: both drivers derive the path as i915/dg2_guc_70.bin (major version only) and only require the major to match. xe_uc_fw_check_version_requirements() fails with -ENOEXEC only if major differs (minor/patch are checked only when full_ver_required, which major_ver entries never set); a blob older than the wanted 70.53.0 loads with drm_notice 'GuC firmware (70.53.0) is recommended, but only (70.x.y) was found' plus 'Consider updating your linux-firmware pkg'; a blob newer than 70.53.0 loads silently, and all other version gates in xe_guc.c/xe_guc_submit.c are minimums (GUC_FIRMWARE_VER_AT_LEAST 70.66, 70.69.0, GUC_SUBMIT_VER >= 1.18.4) that unlock features rather than reject. Hard floor: guc_read_css_info() rejects anything older than 70.29.2. Practical steps: place the blob (Arch ships /usr/lib/firmware/i915/dg2_guc_70.bin.zst, so either replace the .zst with a zstd-compressed copy or install an uncompressed dg2_guc_70.bin, which the kernel prefers), regenerate the initramfs if the module is early-loaded, or point xe.guc_firmware_path / i915.guc_firmware_path at an alternate path (an overridden path also bypasses the version-check fail path). Note sub-70.53 blobs lose version-gated features (e.g. xe disables indirect_ring_state without the 70.53+/compat-1.26 WA 14025515070).
findings.evidence: xe_uc_fw.c doc comment: 'The major version needs to match a major version supported by the driver (if any). The minor version is also checked and a notice emitted to the log if the version found is smaller than the version wanted. This is done only for informational purposes so users may have a chance to upgrade, but the driver still loads and use the older firmware.' Verifier read the function at the v7.3-rc1 tag (byte-identical to master): uc_fw_entry_major_ver expands to { path, a, b, c } with no full_ver_required initialiser; fw_filename_major_ver builds 'i915/dg2_guc_70.bin'; fail: path bypassed when xe_uc_fw_is_overridden(). Lines 352-356: 'Unsupported GuC v%u.%u.%u! v70.29.2 or newer is required'. The zstd/initramfs steps are standard Arch firmware handling inferred from the installed .zst layout, not from a verified claim.

findings.claim: HuC on DG2 under xe is unsupported upstream, so on the A770 xe provides no HuC-dependent media features (VAAPI AVC/HEVC/VP9/AV1 low-power VDEnc encode with CBR/VBR bitrate control), unlike i915 which loads i915/dg2_huc_gsc.bin through the GSC via mei_gsc/mei_pxp. Mainline xe_uc_fw.c's XE_HUC_FIRMWARE_DEFS lists PTL, BMG, LNL, MTL, DG1, ADL-P/S, RKL, TGL only; parse_cpd_header() carries the comment 'We don't support DG2 HuC right now ... just add a reminder in case that changes' followed by xe_assert(xe, xe->info.platform != XE_DG2). On this host under xe, debugfs tile0/gt0/uc/huc_info reports 'HuC firmware: (null) / status: N/A' although dg2_huc_gsc.bin.zst is installed. The only work toward changing this is an out-of-tree '[PATCH v4] drm/xe: add DG2 HuC GSC support and MEI integration' by Daniil Seliverstov (personal gmail, non-Intel; also GitLab drm/xe MR !361), posted 2026-08-02; Patchwork CI refused it (author not allowlisted), it has zero Reviewed-by/Acked-by, the only maintainer reply (Jani Nikula, 2026-08-03) asked the author to stop resending after eight submissions, and no v5 or merge has appeared through September 2026. So the answer to 'will xe ever support HuC on DG2' is: not in mainline today, and the pending effort is stalled, not rejected on technical grounds.

We don't support DG2 HuC right now, so no need to handle it, just add a reminder in case that changes. xe_assert(xe, xe->info.platform != XE_DG2);' — verified in torvalds master, drm-xe-next and drm-xe-fixes. modinfo xe on 7.3.0-rc1-273-tkg-bore lists only dg2_guc_70.bin and dg2_dmc_ver2_08.bin for DG2; modinfo i915 adds dg2_huc_gsc.bin. intel/media-driver README: 'HuC firmware is necessary for AVC/HEVC/VP9/AV1 low power encoding bitrate control, including CBR, VBR, etc.' Patch cover text: 'This enables HuC firmware initialization and authentication on DG2 hardware when using the Xe DRM driver.' findings.claim: xe's scheduler timeout knobs on 7.3-rc1 (verified in the local Kconfig, /proc/config.gz and live sysfs on the A770): CONFIG_DRM_XE_JOB_TIMEOUT_MAX=10000 ms and _MIN=1 ms are absolute bounds on the per-engine-class sysfs job_timeout_ms (and on the runtime-adjustable job_timeout_max), enforced by xe_hw_engine_class_sysfs.c with -EINVAL regardless of privilege; there is no module parameter or exec-queue ioctl property for job timeout, so raising the TDR ceiling above 10 s on the tkg kernel requires rebuilding with a larger CONFIG_DRM_XE_JOB_TIMEOUT_MAX (empirically: echo 10001 > .../engines/ccs/job_timeout_ms -> Invalid argument; 9000 succeeds). CONFIG_DRM_XE_PREEMPT_TIMEOUT=640000 us is the boot-time per-engine-class preemption timeout, runtime-changeable via sysfs preempt_timeout_us within [CONFIG_DRM_XE_PREEMPT_TIMEOUT_MIN=1, _MAX=10000000 us]; xe passes it to GuC as the PREEMPTION_TIMEOUT KLV (so 'jiffy granularity' in the Kconfig label is stale), and a context that does not reach an arbitration point before expiry is hardware-reset. All engine classes on this A770 show defaults 640000/1/10000000, and the user's /usr/local/bin/xe-a770-tune (xe-a770-tune.service) has already raised ccs and rcs preempt_timeout_us to 7500000 (matching i915's CONFIG_DRM_I915_PREEMPT_TIMEOUT_COMPUTE=7500 ms). Important caveat for tuning: exec queues copy job_timeout_ms and preempt_timeout_us from the engine class at creation (xe_exec_queue.c), so sysfs writes affect only queues created afterwards — llama.cpp must be restarted after changing them. The i915 equivalents are CONFIG_DRM_I915_REQUEST_TIMEOUT (20000 ms, i915.request_timeout_ms), HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL 2500 ms and PREEMPT_TIMEOUT_COMPUTE 7500 ms.
findings.evidence: Kconfig.profile help text (Rodrigo Vivi, 'drm/xe: improve Kconfig.profile help text for scheduler timeouts', upstream 5e34374d6531, 2026-06-05, present in /usr/src/linux73-tkg-bore): 'Absolute upper bound (in milliseconds) for the per-engine-class job timeout. This is the maximum value that can be written to the sysfs job_timeout_ms knob, regardless of privileges. To raise this ceiling, increase this value and rebuild the kernel.' and 'Initial per-engine-class preemption timeout ... If the context does not yield before the timer expires, the HW is reset to allow the higher-priority context to execute.' Enforcement predates the help text (commit d27765647297, 2023-08-04). xe_hw_engine.c:539-546 seeds sched_props from XE_HW_ENGINE_JOB_TIMEOUT_MAX / PREEMPT_TIMEOUT macros; CAP_SYS_NICE gate (CONFIG_DRM_XE_ENABLE_SCHEDTIMEOUT_LIMIT=y here) only affects the TIMESLICE ioctl property. Live sysfs at /sys/class/drm/card0/device/tile0/gt0/engines/{bcs,ccs,rcs,vcs,vecs}/ inspected under sudo. A competing claim that the job timeout default is a hardcoded 5000 ms was refuted 0-3. Note the commit carries 'Assisted-by' AI tags, so verifiers validated the code rather than the prose.

findings.claim: The prefill gain (+6-17% dense, +55-62% MoE) and decode slowdown / per-copy latency increase under xe versus i915 on DG2 remain unexplained by verified evidence. Every claim attributing it to GT frequency management (GuC SLPC policy under xe, RPe 750 MHz vs RPn 300 MHz floors, sysfs min_freq/max_freq pinning as a supported way to eliminate ramp latency) was refuted 0-3 and must not be relied on. The only verified structural differences that are candidate contributors are: (a) xe LR-mode submission with user-fence completion (DRM_IOCTL_XE_WAIT_USER_FENCE) instead of dma-fence-backed requests, and no kernel-side implicit sync between execs, which shifts synchronisation cost and ordering to the UMD; (b) preempt-fence based eviction/rebind versus i915's exec-time ww/dma-resv pinning; (c) different scheduler front ends (drm_sched 1:1 + per-queue TDR vs i915_sched_engine) driving the same GuC; and (d) the copy-engine path, since UR_L0_USE_COPY_ENGINE=0 (forcing copies onto the compute queue) removed the bcs stall in the user's own observation. None of these was measured; ULLS/direct submission, immediate command lists, counter-based events and RC6 behaviour did not yield any verified claim.
findings.evidence: Refuted (0-3) claims from the verification pass: 'Under the xe driver, GT frequency is managed by GuC SLPC firmware: the kernel only sets a minimum and maximum ... Frequency ramp behaviour between decode kernels is therefore a firmware policy decision' and 'writing max_freq to a value less than or equal to min_freq turns min_freq into a fixed-frequency request, which is the supported mechanism for eliminating clock ramp latency'. Also refuted (0-3): the assertion that xe VM_BIND on LR VMs forces synchronous bind round-trips that cannot be pipelined, so per-bind latency cannot be cited as the decode penalty either. The structural candidates listed are drawn from confirmed claims [2],[3],[4],[8],[9]; the UR_L0_USE_COPY_ENGINE=0 workaround is the user's own observation stated in the research question and was not independently sourced. This finding is a synthesis of what is and is not established, not a positive result.
findings.vote: n/a — derived from refuted claims (0-3 x3) plus confirmed structural claims

result.caveats: Question (2) is essentially unanswered: all three GT-frequency/SLPC/sysfs-pinning claims and the VM_BIND-latency claim were refuted 0-3, and no claim about ULLS/direct submission, immediate command lists, counter-based events, RC6, PCIe ASPM, or multi-CCS ccs_mode survived, so the report contains no verified explanation for the prefill gain or decode slowdown. Question (4)'s user-mode side (UR_L0_USE_COPY_ENGINE, UR_L0_USE_IMMEDIATE_COMMANDLISTS, UR_L0_USE_DRIVER_INORDER_LISTS, SYCL_PI_LEVEL_ZERO_*, NEO EnableDirectSubmission/DirectSubmissionRelaxedOrdering, ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN, GGML_SYCL_*) and Intel's llama.cpp SYCL.md / oneAPI release-note guidance likewise produced no confirmed claim; the UR_L0_USE_COPY_ENGINE=0 workaround appears only as the user's own observation embedded in the question. No bug report matching the exact DG2 devcoredump (RING_ESR=0x1, IPEHR=0xfffff000, bcs) was found in intel/compute-runtime, intel/llvm, drm/xe gitlab or the kernel lists; the Battlemage #999 analog is a single 12-day-old report with an idle-engine (not execution-error) signature and no Intel diagnosis, and must not be transposed to DG2. Two findings rest on 2-1 votes ([1] USM-BCS timestamp fix, [8] scheduler wording), and [1] is explicitly not applicable to DG2. GuC 70.74.0 has no DG2 field testing outside Intel CI (i915 full CI showed failures on unrelated shards); installing it from intel-staging is unsupported by any distro and the wanted version in both drivers is still 70.53.0. Firmware and patch status are time-sensitive snapshots as of 2026-09-29 (linux-firmware tag 20260916, drm-firmware intel-staging after MR !84, no DG2 HuC v5); lore.kernel.org, patchwork.freedesktop.org and gitlab.freedesktop.org were bot-walled during verification, so mailing-list content was read via the ratatoskr.run mirror and corroborated against GitLab/GitHub primaries. The zstd/initramfs installation details are standard Arch practice inferred from the installed .zst layout, not from a verified source. Several kernel-side statements (LR-mode preempt-fence path, no HuC, BCS0 shared with migrate) are DG2-specific and do not generalise verbatim to Battlemage/Lunar Lake, which have has_usm and their own xe/ firmware directory.
openQuestions: What is the actual mechanism of the DG2 bcs stall under xe (RING_ESR=0x1, IPEHR=0xfffff000): a GuC-never-dispatched context as in compute-runtime #999, a batch execution fault on BCS0 shared between the kernel migrate queue and NEO's copy queue, or a UMD event-ordering gap given that xe adds no kernel-side dependencies for LR-mode execs — and does the intel-staging GuC 70.74.0 or a job_timeout/preempt_timeout change alter it?

What accounts for the decode slowdown and per-copy latency increase under xe on DG2 once frequency-governor explanations are set aside — the user-fence wait path (DRM_IOCTL_XE_WAIT_USER_FENCE) vs i915 dma-fence waits, immediate-command-list flush behaviour on xe, or copy-queue placement — and can it be isolated by measuring with UR_L0_USE_COPY_ENGINE=0/1 and UR_L0_USE_IMMEDIATE_COMMANDLISTS=0/1 under both drivers?

Will Intel bump the wanted DG2 GuC version to 70.74.0 in i915/xe and land it in linux-firmware main (the August test patches and MR !84 suggest intent), and does 70.74.0 (UAPI 1.38.4) change any submission-policy behaviour relevant to LR-mode compute queues on DG2?

Will DG2 HuC support on xe (Seliverstov v4 / drm/xe MR !361) ever be picked up or reworked by an Intel maintainer, or will DG2 users who need VAAPI CBR/VBR low-power encode remain on i915 indefinitely?

refuted.claim: Before this patch, xe's GuC TDR path (check_timeout() in xe_guc_submit.c) treated a job that GuC never actually scheduled by calling xe_sched_invalidate_job(job, 2) and erroring it out, rather than triggering a GT reset; the patch changes that early return to `return true` so the caller resets the GT. This is directly relevant to any 'Timedout job' on a copy-engine queue under xe where the job may never have been picked up by GuC.

For long-running (compute/LR-mode) gpu_vms, the VM_BIND design that xe implements forbids pipelining bind operations behind GPU work: any in-fences must be awaited synchronously inside the ioctl, and LR workloads cannot use dma-fences as out-syncobjs at all. The document states this is a deliberate KMD-simplicity choice, not a dma-fence rule. Consequence for a Level Zero/SYCL stack using LR-mode VMs on xe: each bind/unbind is effectively a synchronous kernel round-trip that cannot be hidden behind queued compute or copy work, which is a plausible per-operation latency cost absent on i915's execbuf/relocation-style model.

On the xe driver the per-engine-class job timeout default is 5000 ms, hardcoded in the driver rather than set by any Kconfig symbol; it can only be changed at runtime through the per-engine-class sysfs knob job_timeout_ms. (This is the threshold after which drm_sched declares a 'Timedout job' and the engine is reset, e.g. the bcs copy-engine reset observed on DG2.)

Linux 6.12.36 (released 2025-07-06) backports upstream commit 0ee54d5cacc0 drm/xe/sched: stop re-submitting signalled jobs, which fixes a bug whose kernel-log signature is exactly the 'Engine reset: engine_class=bcs' + 'Timedout job' + 'Kernel-submitted job timed out' triple on the xe driver's kernel copy/migration queue (guc_id=0, flags=0x13).

Under the xe driver, GT frequency is managed by GuC SLPC firmware: the kernel only sets a minimum and maximum, and GuC is free to request any frequency in that window from PCODE. Frequency ramp behaviour between decode kernels is therefore a firmware policy decision, not a host-side governor the driver tunes directly.

GT frequency can be pinned on xe via sysfs at <device>/tile#/gt#/freq0/: writing max_freq to a value less than or equal to min_freq turns min_freq into a fixed-frequency request, which is the supported mechanism for eliminating clock ramp latency during llama.cpp decode.
